bindings.audiblePhrase: We measure the paper itself. Your enquiry says forty-five centimetres wide, but the print is forty-four. Shall I record forty-four?

responseBinding.questionText: Mount colour: ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: I agree. Please change the order to warm white. I considered pale grey as well, but it makes the sky in the print look dull.

responseBinding.questionText: Frame timber: ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: Let us use Tasmanian oak. I expected to choose black aluminium, yet it feels too severe now that I can see it beside the picture.

responseBinding.questionText: Finish: ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: The honey stain is attractive, but the charcoal finish picks up the dark lines around the lighthouse. Charcoal is my final choice.

responseBinding.questionText: Glazing material: ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: I carry pictures between my flat and my office, so low weight matters more than perfect reflection control. Use acrylic, not ordinary glass.

responseBinding.questionText: Collection date: ______ May

bindings.audiblePhrase: Yes. Could I collect it on Friday the twenty-third instead? I can come before lunch.

responseBinding.questionText: What will keep the print separate from the glazing?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Good. The window mount will keep the print from touching the glazing. A decorative slip is not needed for separation.

responseBinding.questionText: What backing will be used?

bindings.audiblePhrase: We use conservation board behind works on paper. Cardboard is cheaper, but it is not specified for this order.

responseBinding.questionText: What must Eliza bring when she collects the frame?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Friday the twenty-third is available. Bring your order receipt; a photograph of it on your phone is acceptable. You will not need the card used for the deposit.

responseBinding.questionText: What charge is already included in the total?

bindings.audiblePhrase: The wire and two standard hooks are included. The total also includes the fitting fee, so there will not be a compulsory workshop charge added at collection.

responseBinding.questionText: Who checks homes in an assigned area?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Maya Chen covers assigned homes. She checks whether residents received the alert and reports unanswered doors, but she does not enter.

responseBinding.questionText: Who accompanies a resident who requested mobility support?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Owen Patel meets residents who requested mobility help. He accompanies each person along the step-free route until check-in is complete.

responseBinding.questionText: Who sends practice messages to residents?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Lina Brooks updates the noticeboard and sends practice messages. Household questions still go to Maya, not to Lina.

responseBinding.questionText: Who keeps people away from closed streets?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Priya Shah stands at road closures and turns people from unsafe streets. She explains the detour but does not leave the barrier.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the sandbag store?

bindings.audiblePhrase: From the community centre, the step-free route first goes east along Prairie Avenue. Before Willow Street, the municipal garage is on your left. The sandbag store is inside that garage.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the drinking-water station?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Continue east and turn north on Willow Street. At the first crossroads you will see a small plaza. On its west side is the drinking-water station.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the first-aid post?

bindings.audiblePhrase: A little farther north, the library stands on the east side of Willow Street. The covered porch is our first-aid post. The main library doors remain locked during the exercise.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the check-in shelter?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Across from the library is the outdoor rink. Its southern gate is the check-in shelter. Everyone must report there before moving to the final assembly point.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the accessible assembly point?

bindings.audiblePhrase: The accessible assembly point is the raised school yard north-east of the rink. The nearby riverside lookout is lower, so it is not an assembly area.

responseBinding.questionText: Where is the pet holding area?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Residents with pets should use the fenced service yard south-east of the library, beyond the radio booth. The animals stay there with the pet-support helper while owners check in.

responseBinding.questionText: What is the main purpose of worksheet Stage R?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: set expectations about the process and facilitator role

bindings.audiblePhrase: The worksheet calls the opening statement Stage R. Here we outline the process, confidentiality and our impartial role, rather than judging whose evidence is stronger.

responseBinding.questionText: What is the main purpose of worksheet Stage T?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: hear each person's account before asking follow-up questions

bindings.audiblePhrase: Each person’s account is Stage T. We first hear events as that person understands them, saving our follow-up questions until the account has finished.

responseBinding.questionText: What is the main purpose of worksheet Stage K?

bindings.audiblePhrase: The issue summary is Stage K. It establishes the topics needing discussion. In our case, those include music, hallway use and messages through the landlord.

responseBinding.questionText: What is the main purpose of worksheet Stage P?
responseBinding.correctOptionText: discover needs behind their stated demands

bindings.audiblePhrase: Interest exploration is Stage P. We look for practical needs behind stated demands, such as sleep, privacy, predictability or feeling respected.

responseBinding.questionText: What is the main purpose of worksheet Stage M?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Option generation is Stage M. The parties suggest possible approaches, while we postpone any judgment of those ideas until the next stage.

responseBinding.questionText: Documents will be described as ______ rather than proof.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Let us call photographs, notes and messages information rather than proof. They can help clarify events, but we are not deciding a legal case.

responseBinding.questionText: The participants may address each other by their ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: They had already asked to use first names, so we should respect that preference. The useful rule is to speak to one another without insults.

responseBinding.questionText: The disagreement about noise will be placed on the shared ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: We can acknowledge them, but the dispute about noise belongs on the shared agenda whether or not a document settles the date of one incident.

responseBinding.questionText: The trainees will ask what ______ about evenings at home.

bindings.audiblePhrase: A better question is, What matters most about the evenings at home? One neighbour may say sleep, while the other may mention having friends visit.

responseBinding.questionText: Options will be recorded on a ______.

bindings.audiblePhrase: Use a separate sheet for options. Then the agreed agenda remains visible, and we can group similar ideas after the brainstorming stage.

responseBinding.questionText: Before night: amount of stored ______ may affect torpor use

bindings.audiblePhrase: Before night, the amount of stored fuel matters. Researchers often discuss energy reserves when asking whether a bird enters torpor and how long it remains there.

responseBinding.questionText: During torpor: ______ falls substantially

bindings.audiblePhrase: During torpor, metabolic rate falls substantially. The bird uses energy more slowly than it would while maintaining its usual active temperature.

responseBinding.questionText: Body temperature may approach ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: Body temperature also declines. In deeper torpor it may approach ambient temperature, although it remains physiologically regulated rather than becoming an uncontrolled response to cold.

responseBinding.questionText: Main immediate benefit: ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: The immediate benefit is energy savings. A bird can preserve fuel through a long night instead of spending continuously to keep its daytime temperature.

responseBinding.questionText: Rewarming: heat produced largely by ______

bindings.audiblePhrase: Near dawn, the bird must rewarm. Muscle activity produces much of the necessary heat, and this process consumes part of the fuel conserved overnight.

responseBinding.questionText: After activity resumes: ______ can restore reserves

bindings.audiblePhrase: Once active, feeding can restore reserves. Early access to nectar may be important, especially after a cold or lengthy night.

responseBinding.questionText: What feature of darkness may increase the value of torpor?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Let us turn to ecological variation. Night length can extend the period during which no food is available. Longer darkness can therefore increase the value of conserving energy.

responseBinding.questionText: Besides food conditions, what environmental factor changes the energetic challenge?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Air temperature also changes the energetic challenge. A colder environment generally increases the cost of keeping a warm body above its surroundings.

responseBinding.questionText: Which geographical variable distinguished the sites in one Andean study?

bindings.audiblePhrase: One Andean study compared hummingbirds across elevations. Higher and lower sites differed in climate and ecological setting, allowing researchers to examine variation without claiming that elevation was the only cause.

responseBinding.questionText: What should researchers avoid drawing from one population?

bindings.audiblePhrase: Second, avoid species-wide conclusions from one population. Hummingbirds occupy diverse habitats, and closely related species can show different patterns.
